newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iraq's SOMO signs new oil contracts - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's SOMO signs new oil contracts - MEES.

text.p: Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) has signed five new term crude contracts and one spot sale for the second 90-day period of the United Nations oil-for-food deal, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter reported on Monday.

The new term contracts are with India's India Oil Corp (40,000 barrels per day), Cyprus (8,800 bpd), Turkey's Delta (10,000 bpd) and Erden (10,000 bpd) and Japan's Cosmo Oil Co (10,000 bpd), the Cyprus-based MEES reported.
One spot agreement for 1.7 million barrels (19,000 bpd) has been signed with France's Elf Aquitaine.
These new term contracts bring SOMO's total contracts to 30 firms which will lift a total of 642,000 bpd of Iraqi crude in the second 90-day period of the U.N. deal.
"It appears very likely that there are still some possibilities for further sales, term or spot at current prices," MEES reported.
SOMO has agreed with Royal Dutch Shell and Chevron Corp that the two firms would resume original nominations of 30,000 bpd and 20,000 bpd, respectively.
Both had their liftings scaled back in the first 90-day period of the sales plan because of strong oil prices.
